panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Top-left panel shows diffuse erythematous maculopapular rash of abdomen in case-report titled atypical dengue fever with caption stating extensive maculopapular rash spreading throughout entire body. B: Close-up panel shows erythematous maculopapular dengue exanthem consistent with caption of extensive rash throughout body. C: Close-up skin panel shows maculopapular erythema consistent with dengue rash described in caption and in-text upper-limb involvement. D: Hand panel corresponds to caption moderate arthritis on patient's right hand and second right finger in dengue case; diffuse rash context supports dengue exanthem, arthritis noted as proposed finding not in vocabulary. E: Arm panel shows diffuse erythematous rash of upper limb matching caption and in-text dysesthesia and rash of upper limbs in dengue patient.

On the second day (June 10, 2024), she reported dysesthesia in the upper limbs, maculopapular rash (upper limbs, chest, and abdomen), and moderate pruritus. On the third day (June 11, 2024), the rash spread throughout her entire body (Figure 1), accompanied by intense pruritus and myalgia in the abdominal muscles. On the fourth day (June 12, 2024), she developed moderate arthralgia in both hands, and moderate arthritis appeared in the second right finger.
